description: Which states received a systematic month-by-month sweep for a given window, so that a state with no rows in that window can be distinguished from a state nobody looked at. Without this, the two are indistinguishable from the inventory alone.

windows.method: Month-by-month agentic sweep of each state (one research pass per state per month) covering moratorium votes, zoning hearings, legislative action, opposition activity, developer filings, litigation, and utility/grid proceedings. Events were parsed deterministically and converted to inventory candidates only on evidence.

notes.AZ: No local development moratorium found in any Arizona city or county. The only qualifying statewide action was HB 4168 s.31, a freeze on new applications to the state data-center tax relief program, which is out of scope for this inventory and is recorded in state_legislation.csv instead.
notes.coverage_effect: Conversion of a state's sweep can change its count substantially. Florida held 1 inventory row before its sweep was converted and 14 after; Georgia went from 26 to 47; Indiana from 12 to 20. None of these states changed in the world; only our looking did.

windows.field_note: swept_states_with_no_adoptions_in_window means no local instrument was ADOPTED during this window. It does not mean the state has no moratoria at all: Idaho, for example, carries a 2025 Kootenai County instrument in the inventory but adopted nothing new between 2026-05-01 and 2026-07-31.

unswept_caveat: States not listed in swept_states for a window have only opportunistic coverage in that window -- instruments entered the dataset when a researcher working on something else happened to encounter them. Their counts for that window are lower bounds. Cross-state comparison and time-series analysis that includes the window should either be restricted to the swept states or stop at the prior release's cutoff (2026-04-28).
